llm.summary: This package-tracking skill looks safe from a system-access perspective, but it advertises real-time tracking while returning locally invented delivery statuses.

dimensions.detail: Runtime behavior is limited to a local Python CLI using command-line inputs and stdout; however, unvalidated tracking numbers can be reflected into terminal output.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency fetch, remote payload retrieval, or package-install behavior was found in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The script contains an internal demo-data note, but the user-visible tracking output omits that warning and presents fabricated status, location, timeline, and delivery estimates as ordinary tracking results.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, credential access, background workers, memory writes, or system modification behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is real-time package tracking across major carriers, but the implementation only guesses a carrier from patterns and generates synthetic events without contacting any carrier service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you understand this behaves like a demo or mock tracker, not a real parcel-tracking service. Do not use its results for delivery decisions, customer notifications, refunds, or operational workflows unless the publisher replaces the simulation with real carrier lookups or clearly labels every result as simulated.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Confirmed the primary capability mismatch: SKILL.md promises real-time worldwide courier tracking, while scripts/track.py performs only local carrier-pattern detection and simulated timeline generation.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed that the generated shipment events are not sourced from carrier APIs and could mislead users who rely on the displayed delivery status.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded as a security concern: the documentation is mixed Chinese and English and does not contain an instruction forcing the agent to respond only in one language.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed that the module docstring and user-facing skill claims describe tracking, while the code path always generates synthetic results.
[other] unexpected: Confirmed the static scan's integrity concern: fabricated package events are presented in the same format as real tracking output.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a low-severity implementation issue: command-line tracking values are printed without sanitization, allowing terminal or log display manipulation, but not command execution.
